correctness.rationale: The all-index range is finite: 1307 exactly enumerated primitive (p,q) standard representatives, q=2,...,65. A fundamental-parallelogram decomposition gives a certified finite bound for all semigroup indecomposables; scanning all bounded candidates in additive order yields the full Hilbert basis. The toric-surface normalized Nash affine charts are obtained from the boundary of the convex hull of consecutive Hilbert-basis sums as in Atanasov et al., Props. 4.10–4.12. Every primitive chart tangent cone is reduced by exact determinants and extended Euclid, and all nonsmooth descendants are recursively checked. The packaged Python 3 checker, executed against the actual supplied CSV path, regenerated exactly 1307 rows, checked at all 64 indices the claimed bit-length maxima and unique p=q−1 maximizers, and verified the eight-state depth-seven chain. No inference for q>65 or from a partial enumeration is made.

value.rationale: The number of simultaneous normalized Nash rounds is a natural, geometrically intrinsic measure of the complexity of a canonical iterative resolution algorithm for affine toric surfaces. The complete exact determinant-index depth profile through the first seven-round onset is a sharp finite invariant, including the unique extremizer at all 64 determinants and the first seven-step case index 65. The 1307-case exhaustive certificate is neither a random slice nor a mere small one-off calculation: the endpoint is selected by a genuine new resolution-depth phase threshold, and the full smaller-index census certifies minimality. The table supplies a reproducible benchmark for future all-index complexity bounds without presenting a conjectural pattern as an infinite theorem.
